content:
iOS 27.2 is coming soon, bringing a number of new features to iPhone users, including a Messages feature—Suggestions—that appeared in the iOS 27 beta but was subsequently removed.

Messages' "Suggestions" feature was removed during the iOS 27 beta but has now returned in iOS 27.2.

During this summer's iOS 27 beta, one of my favourite AI features was a new addition to Messages that doesn't feel like an AI feature at all: Suggestions.

Here's how Apple officially describes it:

Suggestions appear as small, handy action buttons beneath the messages they're associated with.

As shown below, if someone asks you to do something, you might see a suggestion to add it to Reminders or Notes. If a message mentions an event, Suggestions can let you put it straight into your calendar.

Suggestions worked well for me during the iOS 27 beta, but shortly before the public rollout in the autumn, Apple pushed the feature back to a "future software update".

Now in the iOS 27.2 beta, Suggestions is back. One of the changes may go some way to explaining why it was pulled in the first place.

As I mentioned earlier, Suggestions performed as expected this summer. If I had one criticism, though, it was that it would sometimes pop up in situations where the content of the message really didn't warrant it. Sometimes I'd see suggestions to add things to Notes, Reminders or Calendar when there was no clear reason to do so.

But so far, testing iOS 27.2, I've noticed fewer Suggestions appearing in Messages conversations. When they do appear, the suggestion is clearly justified.

Hopefully the feature will make it into the iOS 27.2 final release in a few weeks' time.

How are you finding Suggestions in iOS 27.2? Share your experience in the comments.
